overview: The board approved a side yard setback variance for a sunroom on Gadsden Street and dimensional variances for a mixed-use redevelopment on High Street. It denied a front yard parking variance on Alexander Street and continued several matters due to pending reviews and lack of quorum.

items.title: 590 Boston Avenue
items.summary: Granted a continuance to the October meeting and a six-month extension of prior relief while the applicant proceeds through Community Development Board review.

items.title: 396 Main Street
items.summary: Noted the applicant's withdrawal of the variance petition to operate a bakery.

items.title: 0 Spring Street
items.summary: Approved a six-month extension of a previously granted variance for modular home construction.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the meeting minutes of May 25, 2023.

items.title: 436 Riverside Avenue
items.summary: Continued the petition for a 10-foot security fence variance to the August meeting so the applicant and staff can consult with the police chief and legal counsel regarding required security plan approvals.

items.title: 16-18 Alexander Street
items.summary: Denied a variance to create a front yard parking space and expand a curb cut, finding the tandem parking conditions did not constitute a unique hardship under the zoning ordinance.

items.title: 39 Gadsden Street
items.summary: Approved a side yard setback variance to replace an existing deck with an enclosed three-season sunroom on the same footprint.

items.title: 15 Hadley Place
items.summary: Continued the hearing on a five-unit residential expansion to August 24, 2023, after a board member recused themselves due to a personal relationship with the applicant, leaving the board without a quorum.

items.title: 421 High Street
items.summary: Approved dimensional variances for front and side setbacks, lot width, lot coverage, and open space to construct a four-story, nine-unit mixed-use building with 10 rear parking spaces.

items.title: Administrative Updates
items.summary: Staff reported on incoming associate board member appointments and a new grant-funded climate planner, and Building Commissioner Bill Forte announced his impending departure.
